findings.highlight: as well as his own choice of "free of desire."
findings.evidenceJa: 望みはない、と告げた言葉をからかうように。
findings.governingReading: The final fragment specifies the priest's words that Gilgamesh appears to mock: his profession of having no desires.
findings.explanation: The English adds amusement at Gilgamesh's own wording. The Japanese keeps his mockery directed at Kirei's claim to have no desires.

findings.highlight: The blond man simply doesn't understand that the priest never had any desires in his life at all.
findings.evidenceJa: 金髪の青年には理解できぬだけで、もとよりこの男に望みなどないのだ。
findings.governingReading: The narration affirms that Kirei has no wish of the kind the Grail would grant; what he has is relentless inquiry.
findings.explanation: Kirei having no wish becomes never having any desires in his life.

findings.highlight: The Holy Grail should respond to its own wishes.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯は己が望みに応えるだけのもの。
findings.governingReading: The Grail is only a machine that answers the user's own desire and manufactures acceptable answers to the user's questions.
findings.explanation: The Grail answering its holder's wishes becomes the Grail responding to its own wishes.

findings.highlight: It is no different from a meal. One should make one's own wishes come true. But this cannot save a human."
findings.evidenceJa: そのようなものは食事と同じだ。願いとは自身を叶えるもの。だが自ら願いを叶えては、人間は救われん」
findings.governingReading: Kirei distinguishes ordinary pleasures from a wish that realizes or fulfills the self; if the person realizes it by their own means, that does not save them.
findings.explanation: A wish fulfilling the self becomes a person fulfilling their own wish.

findings.highlight: ...at a time more than ten years past, when he still waited for his wish to come true.
findings.evidenceJa: もう十年以上も過去となった、まだ望みとやらを持っていた時代の事を。
findings.governingReading: He looks back more than ten years to the period when he still possessed something called a wish.
findings.explanation: A past era when Kirei still had a wish becomes an era of waiting for that wish to come true.

findings.highlight: He was born to a traveling priest in the year 1967.
findings.evidenceJa: 男は１９６７年、父親が巡礼中に授かった子供だった。
findings.governingReading: He was born in 1967 while his father was on religious pilgrimage.
findings.explanation: Kirei's birth during his father's pilgrimage becomes birth to a traveling priest.

findings.highlight: The son excelled at making his father happy. That was probably why his father valued him so.
findings.evidenceJa: 息子が優れているのは、親として喜ぶ事だ。だからこの男は自分を重宝するのだろう。
findings.governingReading: Kirei reasons that a child's excellence is naturally a parental joy, so his father likely values him for that excellence.
findings.explanation: A father valuing an excellent son becomes a son excelling at making his father happy.

findings.highlight: That he could not love his father and was only appeasing his expectations was a separate matter.
findings.evidenceJa: 父を愛せない事と、父の期待に応える事は別の問題だ。
findings.governingReading: Kirei's inability to love his father and his fulfillment of his father's expectations are separate matters.
findings.explanation: Meeting paternal expectations becomes merely appeasing them.

findings.highlight: His father was on a pilgrimage to holy places for over ten years.
findings.evidenceJa: 父は十数年をかけて、茨の踵で聖地を巡礼した。
findings.governingReading: Over more than ten years Kirei's father travels sacred sites with thorn-like suffering at his heels before the moon-distance hyperbole.

findings.highlight: He concluded that such evil could not, should not exist.
findings.evidenceJa: それらが全て、悪は在ってはならぬモノと断定する。
findings.governingReading: Conventional authorities—common sense, moral instruction and justice—collectively declare that such evil should not exist.
findings.explanation: The voices of common sense, morality and justice judging evil become Kirei's own conclusion.

findings.highlight: If such a person could not exist, then why was he born anyway?
findings.evidenceJa: 有ってはならぬモノならば、なぜ、そんなモノが生み出されねばならないのか。
findings.governingReading: Kirei asks why a thing must be produced if it ought not be allowed to exist.
findings.explanation: Something that should not exist becomes something that cannot exist.

findings.highlight: "Where is my sin?" the man kept asking.
findings.evidenceJa: —男は、その罪の所在を問い続けた。
findings.governingReading: The man continues asking where the guilt, fault or responsibility for such an unwanted being's existence is located.
findings.explanation: Asking where responsibility for the existence lies becomes asking where Kirei's own sin is.

findings.highlight: Ten years ago, I sought it out because I wanted to let it exist as it is.
findings.evidenceJa: 十年前聖杯を求めたのも、聖杯が在ろうとしたからだ。
findings.governingReading: Ten years earlier he pursued the Grail because it itself was trying to come into existence/birth.
findings.explanation: The Grail trying to exist becomes Kirei wanting to let it exist.

findings.highlight: No matter what the Holy Grail may be, I bless it for trying to give birth. That is my task."
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯がなんであれ、生まれ出でようとするモノを祝福する。それが私の仕事だからな」
findings.governingReading: Whatever the Grail may be, Kirei blesses the thing that is attempting to be born; he defines this as his vocation.
findings.explanation: Blessing whatever seeks birth becomes blessing the Grail for trying to give birth.

findings.highlight: He is interested in Kirei Kotomine's conclusion—in the end of a man who can only find happiness in the suffering of others.
findings.evidenceJa: 他者の苦しみにしか悦びを見出せなかった言峰綺礼は、此度の結末に関心を持っている。
findings.governingReading: Kirei Kotomine, the man who finds pleasure only in others' suffering, is interested in the present conclusion/outcome.
findings.explanation: Kirei's interest in this war's outcome becomes interest in the ending of Kirei himself.

findings.highlight: If such a being can truly be conceived, that must be...
findings.evidenceJa: もし、本当にそんなものを受胎するというのであらば、或いはそれこそが—
findings.governingReading: If such an unwanted being is truly conceived, Kirei thinks perhaps that may be the thing he seeks.
findings.explanation: A possible answer becomes a necessary answer.
